title: Route Experiments (Console Rollouts) — Beta Program Plan
body:
Doc owner: Talia (Program). Product owner: Marissa (Console & Rollouts).
Last updated: 2025-03-27 (post beta data-quality thread w/ Telemetry + SRE)

1) Summary
Route-level A/B testing (“Route Experiments”) is entering a controlled beta with design partners to validate:
- deterministic assignment + traffic splitting at the routing layer
- experiment attribution integrity across streaming/retries
- Console workflows (create → start/ramp → monitor → stop)
- guardrails + operational readiness (audit logs, RBAC, alerts/runbooks)

This plan covers candidate customers, enablement steps, beta success criteria, support readiness, and the timeline/gates to GA.

2) Beta goals (what we must learn)
Product/UX validation
- Can customers create an experiment correctly without a solutions engineer on every step?
- Do customers understand variant assignment + headers + “stickiness key” requirements?
- Is the results dashboard actionable (deltas + guardrail banners + drill-down) for day-to-day decisions?

Technical validation
- Assignment determinism across regions/restarts (per ADR-047).
- Correct precedence with canary rollouts and fallback policies (routing order consistent).
- Telemetry correctness: attribution drop rate and variance under load, especially for streaming + retries.
- Dashboard query cost under realistic cardinality.

Operational validation
- Guardrail semantics are safe (default soft-stop; optional hard-stop only when explicitly enabled).
- Audit log completeness and export fields satisfy enterprise security review.
- SLO adherence: control plane availability + propagation staleness bounds.

3) In-scope beta features (what customers will see)
- Console: Create experiment wizard (route selection, variant config, traffic split), start/stop/ramp, experiment list + details, results dashboard with deltas + guardrail status.
- Routing layer: deterministic bucketing with supported stickiness key precedence; safe behavior when key missing (warnings + sane default).
- Telemetry: attribution dimensions {route_id, experiment_id, variant_id, model_id, region}; aggregation to power Console charts.
- Guardrails: baseline thresholds (latency p95/p99, error rate, cost per 1K tokens) with soft-stop + notifications; (optional) hard-stop behind kill switch.
- Audit logs: create/update/start/stop (who/what/when, diff summary; redactions).

4) Out-of-scope for beta (explicit)
- “Statistical significance” engine beyond basic deltas and guardrail thresholds.
- Customer-defined custom metrics ingestion.
- Multi-region population rebalancing beyond deterministic bucketing.

5) Candidate customers (beta cohort)
Selection criteria
- Already running production traffic through Redwood routes (or high-fidelity staging)
- Clear use case: model variant comparison, quantization profile comparison, routing policy tuning
- Ability to provide a stable stickiness key (customer_id / end-user id / session id) and work with us on instrumentation
- Willingness to share outcome + feedback weekly during beta

Proposed cohort
A) Design partners (Phase 2 “closed beta”)
1. Acme AI (existing design partner)
   - Primary ask: A/B model variants with latency guardrails + quick rollback
   - Deployment: Dedicated (US + EU)
   - Known risks: multi-region determinism expectations; low tolerance for attribution gaps

2. Northbridge (POC)
   - Primary ask: cost attribution by variant and ability to demonstrate savings
   - Deployment: Hosted API (single region initially)
   - Known risks: security review questions; wants clear exportable evidence

3. Helio Financial (enterprise prospect; security-heavy)
   - Primary ask: audit logging, RBAC, and change management controls
   - Deployment: Private/VPC constraints likely; may run “beta” mostly in staging
   - Known risks: will evaluate compliance posture as much as product functionality

B) “Friendly” internal + partner validation (Phase 1/2)
- Redwood internal dogfooding (Console team + Solutions) on a few production-ish routes with safe traffic caps
- 1–2 additional customer-success managed accounts (TBD) once telemetry/guardrails are stable

6) Beta enablement plan (per-customer)
6.1 Pre-flight checklist (Redwood)
- Feature flags
  - route_experiments_enabled: ON for account + specific regions
  - auto_stop_enabled: OFF by default (soft-stop only)
  - experiment_debug_endpoint: INTERNAL ONLY (support/oncall; RBAC gated)

- RBAC
  - Verify customer roles: who can create/start/stop experiments
  - Confirm break-glass path for stop actions (enterprise admin only)

- Routes + variants readiness
  - Confirm route_id normalization (template vs raw path) to avoid metrics cardinality blow-ups
  - Confirm variant model compatibility with route (context length/tool calling/structured output constraints)
  - Confirm fallback policy interaction for that route is understood (experiment selection happens before fallback evaluation)

- Telemetry readiness
  - Confirm OTel span tags present in staging + prod: experiment_id/variant_id on request span + downstream spans needed for cost/latency rollups
  - Confirm attribution drop rate dashboard in place for this account/route

6.2 Customer-facing enablement steps
Step 1 — Kickoff + use case definition (30–45 min)
- Align on what decision they want to make (quality vs cost vs latency)
- Choose routes (1–2 max) and define “control” vs “treatment” variants
- Define stickiness key source (recommended precedence:
  1) explicit experiment_sticky_key from SDK/API
  2) customer_id
  3) stable end_user_id / session id
  Avoid: IP address, user-agent, random UUID per request)

Step 2 — Setup + access
- Enable feature flag allowlist
- Confirm RBAC role mapping and who will be the day-to-day operator
- Provide docs link + short “do/don’t” guide for stickiness keys

Step 3 — Create experiment in Console (guided first time)
- Configure variants + allocation
- Set guardrails (start with defaults; tighten later)
- Confirm audit trail entries appear as expected

Step 4 — Staged ramp plan
Recommended ramp (can be adjusted by customer risk tolerance)
- Day 0: 1% traffic for 30–60 min
- Day 1: 5% traffic for half day
- Day 2: 10–25% traffic
- Day 3+: 50% traffic if guardrails stable

Step 5 — Weekly review cadence
- Review results deltas, attribution drop rate, and any guardrail events
- Gather UX feedback + missing features
- Confirm next ramp decision and any fixes needed

7) Beta success criteria (GA gate inputs)
Success is defined at three levels: customer outcomes, system correctness, and operational readiness.

7.1 Customer outcomes (must hit for at least 2/3 design partners)
- Customer can independently:
  - create and start an experiment
  - interpret variant deltas and guardrail status
  - stop an experiment safely
- At least one customer uses results to make a real routing decision (switch model/quant profile, adjust policy, or abandon a change with confidence).

7.2 System correctness + data quality (hard gates)
- Deterministic assignment
  - Stable splits within expected error bounds for configured allocations over multi-hour windows
  - No systemic skew when stickiness key is present; clear warnings when absent

- Attribution integrity
  - Attribution drop rate below agreed threshold on beta routes (target: <1% on non-streaming; <2% on streaming; alert if sustained above threshold)
  - Retries/streaming preserve experiment_id/variant_id across request context

- Propagation + staleness
  - Config propagation lag within SLO bounds (no prolonged stale configs; alerts actionable)

- Cardinality + cost
  - No sustained metrics/DB cost spikes from experiment dimensions (dashboards remain responsive; query budgets enforced)

7.3 Operational readiness (hard gates)
- Runbooks complete and on-call trained (SRE + support)
- Alerts tuned (propagation lag, attribution anomalies, “variant 0 traffic”, severe p99 regression)
- RBAC rules enforced + tested (including “stop experiment” permissions)
- Audit logs complete and exportable with required fields (enterprise security review ready)

8) Support readiness checklist
Owner: Support + SRE + Console Tooling. Target completion: before expanding beta beyond design partners.

8.1 Documentation + troubleshooting
- Customer guide published (incl. stickiness key guidance, interpreting variant headers)
- Console tooltips for:
  - variant headers
  - why “missing stickiness key” warnings matter
  - soft-stop vs hard-stop semantics
- Troubleshooting section includes:
  - “my split looks wrong”
  - “results not updating / stale”
  - “streaming requests missing attribution”

8.2 Runbooks and internal tools
- Experiment assignment debugging runbook validated end-to-end
- Internal assignment explain/debug endpoint documented + access path (RBAC gated; redactions)
- Standard dashboards available for Support/SRE (and permissions tested)

8.3 Incident response + escalation
- Define severity policy for:
  - incorrect routing decisions
  - broken guardrails/auto-stop false positives
  - telemetry pipeline regressions triggered by tag/schema changes
- Escalation paths:
  - Control plane/policy engine: Ethan Park / Jordan Lee
  - Console backend/results API: Chloe Martin
  - Telemetry/analytics: Logan Wright / Mei Lin
  - SRE: Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes

9) Known risks + mitigations (beta focus)
- Risk: Missing/low-entropy stickiness key causes skew
  - Mitigation: Console validation warnings; SDK helpers; default precedence rules; recommended keys; block “obviously bad” keys where possible

- Risk: Attribution missing on streaming retries
  - Mitigation: regression tests; verify request-context plumbing in streaming code paths; monitor attribution drop dashboards

- Risk: Config propagation lag → stale experiment config
  - Mitigation: propagation lag metrics + alerts; safe fallback behavior; limit blast radius (traffic caps) during beta

- Risk: Results dashboard query cost spike
  - Mitigation: pre-aggregation; caching; cardinality restrictions; guardrail banners degrade gracefully if results delayed

- Risk: Confusion about guardrails vs auto-stop promises
  - Mitigation: product copy explicitly states soft-stop default; hard-stop is opt-in + kill switch; keep GA messaging aligned

10) Timeline + phases (beta → GA)
Phase 1 — Internal + controlled staging (Feb 2025)
- Feature flag + control plane APIs stabilized
- Router integration behind flag
- Basic attribution + dashboards (internal)

Phase 2 — Closed beta (Mar 2025)
- Enable Acme AI + Northbridge + Helio (staging/limited prod)
- Weekly customer reviews; fix highest-impact gaps
- Implement any required backfills/migrations for attribution schema changes

Phase 3 — Hardening + GA readiness (Apr 2025)
- Alerts tuned, runbooks signed off by SRE
- RBAC + audit logging completeness validated
- GA release train cut + region-by-region enablement plan

GA gate checklist (must be green)
- 2+ design partners successfully ran experiments end-to-end
- Data quality thresholds met (attribution + propagation)
- SRE readiness complete (runbooks/alerts/game day)
- Docs complete + Support trained
- Feature flag rollback plan validated

11) Owners / working cadence
- Weekly beta sync (30 min): Marissa (PM), Dylan/Chloe/Jada (Eng), Logan (Telemetry), Sean/Rafael (SRE), Tessa (Design as needed)
- Customer check-ins: owned by CS/SE with Talia coordinating, Marissa attending key moments (kickoffs, major ramp decisions)

Open questions (to close before expanding beta)
- Do we block overlapping experiments on the same route at GA, or allow with explicit priority? (current direction: block by default; allow internal override)
- What exact default guardrail thresholds should ship for GA across latency/error/cost? (need final SRE sign-off)
- How do we represent “quality” when eval sampling is low (small treatment splits) without misleading customers?

Notes to self / next edits
- Add final list of beta accounts + contacts once enablement email thread locks
- Add links to current dashboards and runbook URLs once PRs are merged into observability pack
